sourceArticle.title: Paper page - OmniRetrieval: Unified Retrieval across Heterogeneous Knowledge Sources
sourceArticle.author: Jinheon Baek ,

athenaOutput.directive: Establish a unified, intelligent retrieval layer within the Creative Liberation Engine that seamlessly accesses and leverages heterogeneous knowledge sources (text, tables, graphs, code) while preserving their native structural affordances and expressive power, presenting a coherent and adaptable user experience.
athenaOutput.rationale: Real-world problem-solving and agent operation demand access to diverse information types. Current retrieval mechanisms are often siloed. Implementing a unified OmniRetrieval capability is critical for the Creative Liberation Engine to operate with comprehensive situational awareness, accelerate agent task completion, and provide a richer, more intuitive user experience for knowledge exploration. This aligns with Article I (Sovereignty) by building core capabilities in-house and Article IV (Quality Standards) by delivering a complete, robust solution.

options.title: The 'Omni-Dispatcher' Agent
options.description: Introduce a dedicated agent (e.g., OMNI_DISPATCHER) responsible for parsing natural language queries, classifying query intent, dynamically identifying relevant knowledge sources (internal wikis, project databases, code repositories, graph stores), translating the query into source-native formats (e.g., SQL, Cypher, vector search queries), dispatching these queries via SIGNAL integrations, and then aggregating/normalizing the diverse results. This approach prioritizes a central orchestration point for retrieval.
options.tradeoffs: High complexity in developing robust query translation and result normalization modules. Requires extensive and evolving SIGNAL integrations for each new knowledge source. Initial setup for source definitions and their capabilities can be intensive. Potential for performance bottlenecks if not optimized for concurrent dispatch.
options.architecture: New OMNI_DISPATCHER agent orchestrated by RELAY/ATHENA; dynamic source registry with capability metadata; query intent classifier (LLM-based); source-native query generators; result normalization/fusion layer; SIGNAL integrations for each knowledge source (e.g., KEEPER for text, custom services for tables/graphs).
options.design: A single, intelligent search bar or conversational interface. Results are presented in a unified feed but with clear visual tagging or iconography indicating the original knowledge source and its type (e.g., 'From Internal Wiki (Text)', 'From Project Database (Table)', 'From CLE Graph (Graph)'). Interactive result cards allow users to 'drill down' into the source-native view if desired, maintaining context.

options.title: Dynamic Knowledge Canvas
options.description: Develop a lightweight RELAY layer that acts as a facade over various knowledge source APIs, exposing detailed metadata about each source's structure and capabilities. The frontend consumes this metadata to dynamically construct query interfaces and result visualizations tailored to the source type. This emphasizes an adaptive and interactive user experience.
options.tradeoffs: Requires significant frontend development for dynamic UI generation and complex state management. Less 'single search bar' and more 'exploratory workspace', which might not suit all user needs. Requires all integrated sources to expose rich, standardized metadata.
options.architecture: RELAY facade service with metadata introspection capabilities for connected sources; standardized API for source metadata; dynamic UI rendering engine on the frontend; API contracts for source-specific query execution and result streaming.
options.design: A 'Knowledge Canvas' where users can visually select or drag-and-drop knowledge source icons. Upon selection, a dynamic query builder (e.g., form-based for tabular data, visual node-editor for graphs) appears. Results are rendered in source-native visualizations (e.g., interactive data grids, network graphs, syntax-highlighted code blocks) within the canvas, allowing for multi-source comparison and interaction through a 'pinboard' or 'workspace' metaphor.

options.title: Semantic Federation Layer
options.description: Implement a semantic layer using an internal ontology (managed by KEEPER) that maps concepts and relationships across heterogeneous sources. A federated query engine (AURORA designed, RELAY implemented) would then translate high-level semantic queries into sub-queries for individual sources, combining and reconciling results based on the ontology. This aims for deeper semantic integration.
options.tradeoffs: High upfront cost and ongoing effort in developing and maintaining a comprehensive internal ontology. Query performance can be complex due to distributed execution, data reconciliation, and inference. Requires careful governance of the semantic model.
options.architecture: AURORA-designed federated query engine; KEEPER-managed internal ontology and semantic mapping service; RELAY for query routing and result orchestration; distributed query planners and optimizers; data reconciliation and fusion logic.
options.design: Users interact with a semantic search interface, allowing natural language queries that leverage inferred relationships (e.g., 'show me all projects related to agent orchestration that involve BOLT'). Results are presented as a coherent, semantically linked knowledge graph fragment or a synthesized answer, rather than raw data. Visualizations would highlight semantic relationships, inferred connections, and the provenance of facts.

options.title: Decentralized Agent-Driven Retrieval
options.description: Instead of a monolithic OmniRetrieval system, empower each specialized agent (e.g., BOLT for code, KEEPER for internal documentation, LEX for legal texts) with its own advanced, source-native retrieval capabilities. ATHENA or RELAY acts as a meta-orchestrator, determining which agent(s) are best suited to answer a given query and then synthesizing their individual responses. This leverages the existing agent ecosystem's expertise.
options.tradeoffs: Consistency in retrieval experience and result presentation across different agents might vary. Requires significant development effort across multiple agents to build out their specialized retrieval skills. Potential for fragmented knowledge if agents do not effectively share or synthesize their findings.
options.architecture: Enhancements to individual agents (BOLT, KEEPER, LEX, etc.) to include source-native retrieval modules; ATHENA/RELAY for meta-orchestration and agent selection based on query intent; standardized inter-agent communication protocols for query passing and result exchange; result synthesis and aggregation layer.
options.design: User experience is primarily conversational and intent-driven, akin to interacting with a 'smart assistant'. The system 'understands' the user's need and implicitly routes to the appropriate agent(s). Results are presented as synthesized, agent-specific insights rather than raw data dumps, potentially with clear attribution to the agent that provided the information. Micro-interactions would guide users through multi-agent dialogues.

options.title: Hybrid Contextual Retrieval Pipeline
options.description: Implement a multi-stage retrieval pipeline that first performs a broad semantic search (e.g., using vector embeddings via KEEPER) to identify relevant documents/chunks, then, if contextually appropriate, applies structured query generation (e.g., SQL/Cypher) to extract precise facts from identified structured sources. An LLM (via SIGNAL integration) acts as a query intent classifier and result synthesizer, determining the optimal retrieval path for each query.
options.tradeoffs: Complex pipeline orchestration and result fusion logic. Requires robust LLM integration for intent classification and synthesis, which can have latency, cost, and explainability implications. Tuning the hand-off between semantic and structured retrieval can be challenging.
options.architecture: KEEPER-enhanced vector database for semantic search; LLM-based query intent classifier (SIGNAL integration); structured query generator (SQL, Cypher); result fusion and ranking algorithm; pipeline orchestration engine.
options.design: A single search bar. Results are intelligently blended and ranked, with clear indicators of the retrieval method used (e.g., 'Semantic Match (Text)', 'Exact Match (Table)', 'Inferred from Graph'). Users can optionally filter results by retrieval method or source type. Visualizations might combine text snippets with tabular data excerpts or graph visualizations, dynamically adapting to the blended result set.

options.title: Creative Liberation Engine Knowledge Lakehouse with Query Views
options.description: Establish a unified 'Knowledge Lakehouse' as the primary data ingestion and storage layer for *all* Creative Liberation Engine data, regardless of original structure. Data is stored in open, standardized formats. Instead of directly querying raw data, create 'query views' (materialized or virtual) that expose source-native structures (tables, graphs, document collections) *on top* of the lakehouse. This centralizes storage while preserving native query access.
options.tradeoffs: Significant infrastructure investment in building and maintaining the lakehouse. Requires careful schema design for views to genuinely preserve source affordances without homogenization. ETL complexity for diverse data ingestion.
options.architecture: AURORA-designed Knowledge Lakehouse architecture (e.g., Delta Lake); BOLT-implemented ETL pipelines for heterogeneous data ingestion; data catalog for managing schema and metadata; virtual or materialized query view engine exposing SQL, Cypher, or document-like interfaces over the lakehouse.
options.design: A unified data catalog interface where developers and advanced users can browse available knowledge views, understand data lineage, and inspect view definitions. For end-users, the 'Omni-Dispatcher' (or similar agent) would query these views. The design emphasizes data governance, discoverability, and the ability to visualize the underlying data structure and its transformations through the views.
